title: The Loop Is the Product — Roland Gavrilescu, Introspection
talk_summary: Roland Gavrilescu argues that the durable asset in agent systems is the loop plus a versioned 'recipe' (harness, evals, prompts, tools, model profiles) that captures human taste and is continuously distilled from production traces. He proposes turning failure patterns into judges/evals, repeated behavior into skills/prompts, and measuring 'valued work per watt' as the optimization score.

takeaways.what_they_do: Mine production traces for recurring failure patterns and user frustration clusters, then have agents write judges/evals for each pattern; humans only calibrate the judgment, not build the eval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Failure patterns should become judges and evals. Repeated behavior should become skills and prompts.

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents generate the eval/judge code; a human reviews and signs off on the judgment ('do you agree this is good?'), keeping taste human but labor cheap.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You don't need the human to actually build the evals. You need them to calibrate the evals.

takeaways.what_they_do: Package harness config, evals, prompts, tool choices, and per-model profiles into a git repo owned by the company, provider-agnostic, so changes are diffable and portable across models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's something that you control lives in your company and is agnostic to the models and providers you use.

takeaways.technique: Valued work per watt as the score
takeaways.what_they_do: Measure value delivered per unit of compute/token spend, and treat economic viability as a first-class optimization after reaching quality frontier.
takeaways.evidence_quote: How much value am I getting per watt?

takeaways.what_they_do: Run a separate loop over the artifacts of the first loop (traces, diffs, outcomes) to decide what to change in harness/evals/prompts, rather than only running workers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: How you look at the artifacts and know what to change is the taste.

takeaways.technique: Offline evals then prod A/B promotion
takeaways.what_they_do: Validate recipe candidates offline against evals, then confirm with real users via A/B or multi-arm bandit before promoting a new agent version.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The test here is when you go to prod. So, do the end user agree with your taste
